title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: A change in the mean and/or variability of the climate that persists for decades or longer, from natural or human causes (IPCC).

en.text: Climate change has external causes (incoming solar radiation, atmospheric composition, the Earth's surface) and internal ones. Natural drivers include Milankovitch cycles, solar output and sulfur-rich volcanic eruptions; human activities, mainly burning fossil fuels, are now the primary cause, and global temperature has risen about 1 °C since the late 1800s. Models project more warming, more water vapour, extreme rain, worse droughts, faster sea-ice melt and rising seas. The world responds with mitigation and adaptation, agreements from Toronto to Kyoto and Paris, and in Ethiopia the CRGE strategy.

screens.title: Warm up: cause, consequence or response?
Unit summary
paras: External causes: changes in incoming solar radiation, the atmosphere's composition, the Earth's surface.
Milankovitch: small changes in tilt and orbit → glacial and interglacial episodes.
Solar output changes and sulfur-rich eruptions can also change climate.
People emit vast amounts of GHGs; temperature has risen about 1 °C since the late 1800s.
Models: more water vapour, extreme rain, worse droughts, faster sea-ice melt, rising seas.
Responses: mitigation, adaptation, international agreements, Ethiopia's CRGE.
